what_it_is.prose: Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) does not market a single integrated 'CUAS' product under that name; rather, TASL's counter-UAS-relevant capability spans multiple divisions and product lines. The Rajak ULR 50 EO/IR surveillance system can detect small drones at 10 km+, vehicles at 50 km+, and humans at 40 km+. The TASL Surface Surveillance Radar (SSR) is an X-band 8-12 GHz system listed as CUAS-capable. A May 2026 TASL white paper titled 'Integrated Anti-Drone System: Powered by EO/IR Sensors, AI Processing, and C2 with Fire Control Integration' describes TASL's architectural approach. Notably, no public record of an integrated TASL CUAS product deployed with Indian forces has been found. TASL's Unmanned Aerial Systems division produces the Sky-I, Rakshak VTOL, and Advanced Loitering Systems (ALS) UAVs, but these are platforms rather than counter-platforms. The 'V1' label used in the Atlas should be treated as an editorial designation pending vendor confirmation of a specific product.

deployments_procurement.summary: No public procurement or deployment records for a TASL CUAS system have been found. TASL UAVs (Sky-I, Rakshak VTOL, ALS) are in service or under trial with Indian forces, but these are unmanned platforms rather than counter-UAS systems. The Rajak ULR 50 was unveiled in 2026 but no customer has been named.
